report_name: Cloud Misconfigurations Persist as Major Breach Vector in 2026

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: A cloud application platform exposed 38 million records from 47 customers because a service was configured with a default setting that made data publicly accessible, which aligns with data being exposed from cloud storage due to improper permissions.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: A cloud data platform provider suffered a breach impacting 165 customers after attackers used stolen credentials to log in. The provider did not enforce MFA, making the stolen cloud account credentials sufficient for access.

indicators.name: AWS S3 Public Access Block Disabled
indicators.pattern:
title: AWS S3 Public Access Block Disabled
id: 2b9a1c8d-4e5f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects when the Public Access Block configuration for an S3 bucket is modified to be less restrictive, potentially exposing data. This aligns with misconfigurations leading to data exposure as described in recent incidents.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/08/why-cloud-misconfigurations-continue-to-cause-data-breaches-in-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.collection
level: high
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventName: PutBucketPublicAccessBlock
    requestParameters.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicAcls: 'false'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects modifications to AWS S3 bucket public access settings that make them less restrictive, a common vector for data exposure through cloud misconfiguration.

indicators.name: AWS IAM AdministratorAccess Policy Attachment
indicators.pattern:
title: AWS IAM AdministratorAccess Policy Attachment
id: f8a7b6c5-d4e3-4f2a-1b9c-8d7e6f5a4b3c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the attachment of the highly permissive 'AdministratorAccess' policy to an IAM role. This can be an indicator of privilege escalation or a misconfiguration granting excessive permissions.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/08/why-cloud-misconfigurations-continue-to-cause-data-breaches-in-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1098.003
  - attack.privilege_escalation
level: high
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventName: AttachRolePolicy
    requestParameters.policyArn: 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the attachment of the AWS IAM 'AdministratorAccess' policy, which grants full administrative privileges and represents a significant security risk if misconfigured.
